messages.subject: Non-stationary Poisson Process
parts:
I have been scouring the vignettes and reference material to understand how Simmer deals with non-stationary (or non-homogeneous) arrival processes. I have yet to see any information on (1) how to implement a non-stationary arrival process or (2) the method used to generate non-stationary arrivals. 

Before I spend a day running tests or writing a personalized (and therefore inevitably inefficiency) thinning process, I wanted to see if anyone can point me in the right direction.

Thanks in advance,
David

On Wed, 20 Jan 2021 at 17:47, David Rea <drea...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have been scouring the vignettes and reference material to understand how Simmer deals with non-stationary (or non-homogeneous) arrival processes. I have yet to see any information on (1) how to implement a non-stationary arrival process or (2) the method used to generate non-stationary arrivals.

One of the strengths of simmer (in my opinion) is that the simulation engine is completely process-agnostic. You can either implement your own arrival process as an R function (inside this function, you can rely on standard R functions, other packages, call compiled code...; and also you can query the simulation time, the state of resources, attributes...) and feed it to add_generator, or take a bunch of arrivals from any source (e.g., experimental ones) and feed them to add_dataframe.
 
--
Iñaki Úcar
